records.title: A Survey for LLM Agent Trajectory Analysis: From Failure Attribution to Enhancement
records.rationale: Abstract text is only IEEE metadata, but the title is unambiguous: a TSE survey of agent trajectory analysis organized around failure attribution, which is exactly the failure-mode taxonomy and measurement question in RQ3.

records.title: Benchmarking and Studying the LLM-based Agent System in End-to-End Software Development
records.rationale: Explicitly builds a benchmark for end-to-end software development and isolates the effect of configuration choices, naming 'single-agent versus multi-agent' as a studied factor, which is the direct empirical comparison RQ2 asks for.

records.title: Llm-based multi-agent systems: Frameworks, evaluation, open challenges, and research frontiers
records.rationale: Secondary study covering LMAS frameworks, evaluation practice, open challenges, and frontiers, and the snippet references a direct architectural comparison; this maps onto RQ1's coverage of evaluation, reliability, and future work.

records.title: ALMAS: an Autonomous LLM-based Multi-Agent Software Engineering Framework
records.rationale: Only IEEE metadata is available, but the title names a concrete autonomous multi-agent SE framework, i.e. the role-specialized orchestration architecture class that RQ1 and RQ2 are about; the full text is needed for its role decomposition and evaluation.

records.title: Agentware in software engineering: A taxonomy for leveraging llms-based multi-agent systems
records.rationale: Provides an SE-specific taxonomy for LLM multi-agent systems and counts the literature by configuration (it notes 34 papers proposing single-agent systems), giving the architectural landscape and single-versus-multi framing that anchors RQ1.

records.title: Is Collaboration Worth It? A Decision-Oriented Survey in Multi-Agent Systems
records.rationale: The framing question is literally when multi-agent collaboration is worth its cost relative to a comparable single-agent pipeline, including latency overheads and specialized-role designs, which is RQ2 stated as a survey.

records.title: Assessing and Enhancing the Robustness of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems Through Chaos Engineering
records.rationale: Applies chaos engineering to LLM multi-agent systems, which yields both an injection-based measurement method and observed robustness breakdowns; this is a direct source for RQ3's failure modes and how they are measured.

records.title: A Comparative Study Towards Designing a Hybrid Architecture of Microservices and LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
records.rationale: Compares microservice architecture against LLM multi-agent design to propose a hybrid, so it contributes architectural design guidance and coupling considerations rather than evidence on single-agent versus multi-agent task performance.

records.title: Methods and Techniques of Agentic Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review
records.rationale: An SLR of agentic SE methods and techniques covers the primary-study population underlying RQ1, and its inclusion set and categorization should be read in full to check coverage of this review's own corpus.

records.title: THE CAPABILITIES AND LIMITATIONS OF AI AGENTS IN SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT
records.rationale: The fragmentary snippet does discuss specialized LMAs and multi-agent versus single-agent architectures in software development, but it reads as a secondary overview with no identifiable venue or original evidence, so it supports rather than settles RQ2.

records.title: An LLM-based multi-agent framework for agile effort estimation
records.rationale: A named multi-agent framework applied to an SE planning activity (agile effort estimation) at ASE; it supplies an architecture and task-specific evaluation, but estimation is peripheral to the code generation, repair, and verification focus of the RQs.

records.title: "ENERGY STAR" LLM-Enabled Software Engineering Tools
records.rationale: Measures real-time energy consumption and inference time of LLM code generation across model sizes with a RAG plus prompt-engineering pipeline, supplying the sustainability measurement method RQ1 mentions, though it studies single models rather than agent orchestration.

records.title: Safe and Scalable Collaboration in Multiagent LLM Systems: A Comprehensive Review
records.rationale: Reviews safety and scalability of multiagent LLM collaboration and flags that comparative analysis is hampered by missing baselines, which is a generalizable measurement critique for RQ3 even though the review is not SE-specific.

records.title: Thucy: An LLM-based Multi-Agent System for Claim Verification across Relational Databases
records.rationale: A multi-agent claim-verification system over relational databases benchmarked on TabFact against prior state of the art, with no single-agent ablation and no software engineering task; useful only as background on evidence-producing agent pipelines.

records.title: PhishDebate: An LLM-Based Multi-Agent Framework for Phishing Website Detection
records.rationale: Outside software engineering, but it reports a clean quantitative comparison of a four-role debate architecture against single-agent and chain-of-thought baselines, which is admissible cross-domain evidence for when role specialization plus debate helps under RQ2.

records.title: Towards A Sustainable Future for Peer Review in Software Engineering
records.rationale: Concerns scholarly peer review of SE research papers and reviewer supply, not LLM agents performing a software engineering activity; the mention of AI tools is incidental to a community-process position paper.

records.title: When Code Becomes Abundant: Redefining Software Engineering Around Orchestration and Verification
records.rationale: Position paper arguing SE must recenter on orchestration, architectural control, and systematic verification under AI automation, and it names accountability collapse as the central risk, which frames the verification and sustainability strands of RQ1.

records.title: Impostor Phenomenon as Human Debt: A Challenge to the Future of Software Engineering
records.rationale: A human-factors position paper on psychological safety and inclusion in the SE workforce with no LLM agents, architecture, or empirical agent evaluation; out of scope for all three RQs.

records.title: Multi-Agent LLM Orchestration Achieves Deterministic, High-Quality Decision Support for Incident Response
records.rationale: 348 controlled trials directly contrasting single-agent copilot against multi-agent orchestration on identical incident scenarios, with a new Decision Quality metric and a latency-versus-quality finding; this is exactly the operations-side evidence and measurement instrument RQ2 and RQ3 need, notwithstanding implausibly extreme headline ratios that warrant full-text scrutiny.

records.title: How Software Engineering Research Overlooks Local Industry: A Smaller Economy Perspective
records.rationale: Thematic analysis of a community survey about the research-industry gap in smaller economies; contains no LLM agents and no software engineering task evaluation.

records.title: Large Language Model-Based Agents for Software Engineering: A Survey
records.rationale: The anchor survey mapping LLM-based agents onto software engineering activities, contrasting agents against standalone LLMs; it is the reference frame for RQ1's landscape and must be read in full to align this review's categories.

records.title: Large language model agents: A comprehensive survey on architectures, capabilities, and applications
records.rationale: General-purpose agent survey that explicitly performs a systematic architecture comparison and reports multi-agent gains over single-agent baselines, giving cross-domain RQ2 signal without any software engineering specificity.

records.title: Bridging the Gap: Adapting Evidence to Decision Frameworks to support the link between Software Engineering academia and industry
records.rationale: About evidence-based SE methodology and transferring SLR findings to practitioners; it neither studies LLM agents nor compares agent configurations, so it falls outside the inclusion criteria.

records.title: Maintaining the Heterogeneity in the Organization of Software Engineering Research
records.rationale: An essay on funding models and the organization of the SE research community; no LLM agents, architecture, or empirical results relevant to any RQ.

records.title: MULTI-AGENT SYSTEM FOR AUTOMATED CODE REVIEWS
records.rationale: Proposes a multi-agent LLM code review system motivated explicitly by single-agent limitations and closes with a comparative synthesis of gaps, placing it squarely on RQ2 for the code review activity; grey-literature thesis status is flagged, not disqualifying.

records.title: Comparative evaluation of future collider options
records.rationale: Particle physics report comparing CERN collider proposals; matched only on the words comparative, evaluation, and sustainability, making it a clear keyword collision.

records.title: Small LLMs Are Weak Tool Learners: A Multi-LLM Agent
records.rationale: Decomposes an agent into planner, caller, and summarizer roles and shows the multi-LLM configuration surpasses the equivalently trained single-LLM agent, especially for smaller models; that is a concrete condition under which role specialization wins, which is the mechanism RQ2 targets, so it is promoted despite its low rank and non-SE benchmarks.

records.title: A Mosaic of Perspectives: Understanding Ownership in Software Engineering
records.rationale: Examines psychological and organizational ownership in agile teams; no LLM agents and no agent architecture or evaluation, so it does not meet the inclusion criteria.

records.title: TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework
records.rationale: A well-known role-specialized debate architecture (analysts, bull/bear researchers, risk team) but in financial trading, and its reported superiority is over trading baselines rather than a matched single-agent LLM, so it serves only as background on specialization patterns.

records.title: Towards Effective GenAI Multi-Agent Collaboration: Design and Evaluation for Enterprise Applications
records.rationale: Benchmarks coordination and routing protocols with quantified deltas over single-agent approaches, a 23% gain specifically on code-intensive tasks, and an orchestration-bypass latency tradeoff; that combination speaks directly to RQ2 conditions and RQ3 coordination measurement.

records.title: What Does a Software Engineer Look Like? Exploring Societal Stereotypes in LLMs
records.rationale: Studies gender and racial bias in LLM-generated recruitment profiles and images for SE roles; it concerns social bias rather than agents performing software engineering tasks.

records.title: Promptware Engineering: Software Engineering for Prompt-Enabled Systems
records.rationale: Roadmap for treating prompts as software artifacts across the lifecycle; relevant background on the non-determinism that complicates agent verification, but it proposes no agent architecture, benchmark, or configuration comparison.

records.title: The Future of AI-Driven Software Engineering
records.rationale: Vision paper on human-AI symbiosis in software development and the research challenges it raises; useful for framing future-work discussion but it offers no agent-level evidence or failure-mode analysis to synthesize.
